content.text: I reviewed every input file, every draft section, the numeral ledger, and all five figure briefs, and built a full source ledger from the disclosure and the single USER passage in the conversation.

input.summary:
Full ledger review completed against input/disclosure.md and the one USER passage in input/conversation.md (input/brief.md used only for title, applicant/inventor, no-priority and no-government-support formalities; the "YOU" passage, which asserts a "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface," was treated as context only and correctly appears nowhere in the draft; input/request.md is a repair instruction and affirms no technical content).

Claims: all 17 claims (independent 1, 11, 14) were traced limitation by limitation. Two semicircular frame halves, hinge end/latch end, releasable latch, three jaw carriages, radial guides, pivoting concave jaw pads, "without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter," outward carriage springs, cam ring retained in an annular guide, segmentation with one segment carried by each frame half, complementary drive faces at the hinge end and the latch end coupling the segments on closure and separating on opening, followers in respective oblique slots, wedge on the latch bearing on a ring drive face, rotation through a limited stroke, synchronized/equal inward travel, first holding position and second over-center position, force-limiting spring stack between latch handle and wedge taking up remaining latch travel after all pads contact, indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing at a predetermined compression range, non-diameter-measuring indication, mounting boss outside the annular guide for a sensor, tool or conduit that does not participate in jaw synchronization, and the install/release method steps each trace to an exact affirmative sentence of the disclosure. Equal inward travel (claims 6, and description) traces to "synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages" read with "rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others." "Wedge carried by the releasable latch" traces to "a force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge." Claim 11's "installed clamp assembly" combination is supported by the clamp-on-pipe disclosure and is antecedently defined in the description. Antecedent basis, dependency chain, statutory classes, absence of means-plus-function language, and the 137-word abstract were checked.

Numerals: the ledger's 28 entries (10–66, with 28 unused) were cross-checked three ways — every ledger numeral appears in the description, every numeral in each figure's front matter matches that figure's placement targets and its "Numerals shown" list, and no numeral is used for two different parts. Segment/face assignments are internally coherent: hinge at the left break in FIGS. 1–3, latch at the right, 44/48 on the upper first segment 32 carried by first frame half 12, 46/50 on the lower second segment 34 carried by second frame half 14, with the three slots and three carriages at matching angular stations across FIGS. 1, 2, 3 and 5.

Figure briefs: each geometric and relational statement was tested for undisclosed technical substance. The FIG. 3 abutting end faces are expressly left shape-neutral; the ring drive face 54 is "short plain" (no taper, angle, depth or runout stated) and its latch-end circumferential station is entailed by the disclosed latch-carried wedge; the common rotational sense of the three oblique slots is entailed by "synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages"; the FIG. 4 fixed edge 60 and the pin projecting past the housing wall are entailed by "a visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing"; the mounting boss drawn radially outboard of the channel traces to "outside the annular guide." No brief states proportions, materials, counts beyond three carriages/three slots/two segments, or contact topology that is absent from the source. No "by way of example," "any closed outline," or other embodiment-broadening justification leaked from a brief into the Brief Description or the description; the "depiction convention" language stays inside the briefs. No section lines are designated in any view (FIG. 2 is a near-side-omitted interior view and FIG. 4 a cutaway), so there is no cross-view section-designation mismatch to reconcile. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains in any application section.

One minor issue is reported: the jaw carriage rectangle (FIGS. 1, 2, 5), the FIG. 2 slideway outline, and the FIG. 2 jaw pad are generic outlines that are not covered by the "shown schematically" sentence those same briefs apply to every other appearance-undisclosed part, including the pad in FIGS. 1 and 5. The fix is a labeling correction only; no geometry, embodiment, or claim text changes.

findings.title: Jaw carriage outline (and, in FIG. 2, the slideway and jaw pad) drawn as a generic shape without the "shown schematically" designation applied to every comparable part
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, figures/FIG-2.md and figures/FIG-5.md — the "Geometry to draw" bullets for the carriage/slideway/pad and the closing schematic-designation sentence of each brief
findings.detail: The disclosure discloses the carriage's function but not its appearance: "Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad." The three briefs choose a rectangle for the carriage and parallel radial lines for the guide, which is a permissible depiction convention because it adds no undisclosed relationship — the radial long dimension and "narrower than the slideway" both follow directly from sliding in a radial guide, and the pad's concave inner edge and small-circle pivot are affirmatively disclosed. The defect is only that the gating designation is applied inconsistently: FIG. 1 designates "the hinge, the latch, the small blocks at the inner ends of the carriage blocks, and the mounting boss" schematic but not the carriage blocks; FIG. 2 designates "The band, the channel, the followers, the springs and the small rectangular projection" schematic but not the carriage, the slideway or the pad, even though FIGS. 1 and 5 both designate that same pad schematic; FIG. 5 designates "The pad, follower, slot, and spring" schematic and the frame portion schematic but not the carriage. The same part is therefore labeled a convention in one brief and left undesignated in another, so an undisclosed outline is left standing as an unqualified assertion. This is a labeling correction; no geometry, embodiment or claim text may change, and no shape or optional embodiment should be added to the application text to justify the outline.
findings.evidence: FIG-1.md: "Three carriage blocks at roughly equal angular intervals ... Each is a small rectangle whose long dimension is radial" and "The hinge, the latch, the small blocks at the inner ends of the carriage blocks, and the mounting boss are shown schematically." | FIG-2.md: "In each slideway a carriage drawn as a radially long rectangle narrower than the slideway" ... "On the inner end of each carriage a pad drawn as a small block with a concave inner edge, joined to the carriage at a small circle." ... "The band, the channel, the followers, the springs and the small rectangular projection are shown schematically." | FIG-5.md: "A carriage drawn as a radially long rectangle narrower than the slideway, centered in the slideway." ... "The pad, follower, slot, and spring are shown schematically." | Disclosure (nearest affirmative passage, function only, no appearance): "Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter."
findings.fix: Edit only the schematic-designation sentences of the three figure briefs, leaving all geometry bullets, numerals and application text unchanged. In figures/FIG-1.md replace "The hinge, the latch, the small blocks at the inner ends of the carriage blocks, and the mounting boss are shown schematically." with "The hinge, the latch, the carriage blocks, the small blocks at the inner ends of the carriage blocks, and the mounting boss are shown schematically." In figures/FIG-2.md replace "The band, the channel, the followers, the springs and the small rectangular projection are shown schematically." with "The slideways, the carriages, the pads, the band, the channel, the followers, the springs and the small rectangular projection are shown schematically." In figures/FIG-5.md replace "The pad, follower, slot, and spring are shown schematically." with "The carriage, pad, follower, slot, and spring are shown schematically."
